title: HIV prevention drug could reduce cases globally but USAID cuts prevent access, say experts

claims.claim_text: New innovations in HIV prevention could dramatically reduce the number of new HIV cases around the globe.
claims.subject: Innovations in HIV prevention
claims.attributed_source: experts at the Aids 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

claims.claim_text: US foreign aid cuts will mean that those that most need the new medication will be unable to access it.
claims.subject: US foreign aid cuts impact on access to new medications
claims.attributed_source: experts at the Aids 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

claims.claim_text: One year ago, the World Health Organization recommended that governments around the world prioritize expanded access to lenacapavir, an injectable version of the HIV prevention medication PrEP that requires only two injections annually.
claims.subject: World Health Organization (WHO)

claims.claim_text: PrEP is 99% effective in preventing sexually transmitted HIV for people who take it consistently.
claims.subject: PrEP effectiveness

claims.claim_text: Access to lenacapavir is limited outside clinical trials.
claims.subject: Access to lenacapavir

claims.claim_text: The WHO recommended that governments around the world prioritize scaling up availability of the injectable medication lenacapavir, because it could be gamechanging for populations that face considerable barriers to access for the medications currently available.
claims.subject: World Health Organization (WHO) recommendation on lenacapavir

claims.claim_text: For people who face poverty or stigma, or who live in rural areas far from healthcare services, accessing a daily pill or an every-other-month injection can be close to impossible.
claims.subject: Barriers to accessing current HIV prevention medications

claims.claim_text: Lenacapavir would provide strong protection against HIV while only requiring patients to access healthcare twice annually.
claims.subject: Lenacapavir HIV protection and healthcare access frequency

claims.claim_text: A mathematical modeling study from the WHO and the United Nations estimated that widespread availability of lenacapavir could prevent 41% of new HIV infections in South Africa, Zimbabwe and western Kenya.
claims.subject: Effectiveness of lenacapavir in preventing new HIV infections
claims.attributed_source: a mathematical modeling study from the WHO and the United Nations

claims.claim_text: When the WHO recommended global investment in lenacapavir for HIV prevention in 2025, the Trump administration was already in the process of dissolving USAID.
claims.subject: Trump administration dissolving USAID during 2025 WHO recommendation
claims.attributed_source: a study in the Lancet Global Health

claims.claim_text: USAID provided 73% of donor-funded resources for HIV prevention globally.
claims.subject: USAID's contribution to donor-funded HIV prevention resources
claims.attributed_source: a study in the Lancet Global Health

claims.claim_text: As of July 2026, multiple reports show that investment in HIV prevention has declined dramatically around the world.
claims.subject: Global investment in HIV prevention as of July 2026

claims.claim_text: Funding cuts are affecting the delivery of new HIV prevention technologies as well as decreasing the number of people engaged in care and prevention services.
claims.subject: Impact of funding cuts on HIV prevention and care
claims.attributed_source: Beatriz Grinsztejn, president of the International Aids Society

claims.claim_text: The funding cuts affect not only the availability of medications but also the ability of organisations to reach the people who need them.
claims.subject: Effects of funding cuts on medication availability and outreach

claims.claim_text: When funding cuts came, peer outreach workers were one of the biggest impacted groups.
claims.subject: Impact of funding cuts on peer outreach workers
claims.attributed_source: Ailish Brennan, a policy analyst at Harm Reduction International

claims.claim_text: Peer outreach workers are crucial to reaching people who use drugs, building their trust, and engaging them with services.
claims.subject: Role of peer outreach workers in HIV prevention
claims.attributed_source: Ailish Brennan, a policy analyst at Harm Reduction International

claims.claim_text: People who inject drugs are at a particularly high risk for contracting HIV, especially if they do not have access to clean syringes.
claims.subject: HIV risk among people who inject drugs
claims.attributed_source: a report from the International Network of People Who Use Drugs

claims.claim_text: Organisations were most likely to respond to loss of funding by cutting outreach services.
claims.subject: Organisations' response to funding loss
claims.attributed_source: a report from the International Network of People Who Use Drugs

claims.claim_text: Many harm reduction and HIV prevention organisations around the world were having to shut down locations, including mobile locations.
claims.subject: Closure of harm reduction and HIV prevention organisation locations
claims.attributed_source: Ailish Brennan, a policy analyst at Harm Reduction International

claims.claim_text: Clients at risk for HIV lose trust in organisations when harm reduction and prevention service locations shut down.
claims.subject: Effect of service location closures on client trust
claims.attributed_source: Ailish Brennan, a policy analyst at Harm Reduction International

claims.claim_text: If clients have to travel further to receive services, they lose their local point of contact.
claims.subject: Impact of increased travel distances on clients
claims.attributed_source: Ailish Brennan, a policy analyst at Harm Reduction International

claims.claim_text: Innovations like long-acting injectables will not reach the people who need them most due to funding cuts and service reductions.
claims.subject: Impact of funding cuts on access to long-acting injectable HIV prevention
claims.attributed_source: Ailish Brennan, a policy analyst at Harm Reduction International

claims.claim_text: Before the dissolution of USAID, much of Latin America had been left out of agreements with US-based pharmaceutical companies to make innovative HIV prevention more affordable.
claims.subject: Latin America's exclusion from pharmaceutical agreements
claims.attributed_source: Beatriz Grinsztejn, president of the International Aids Society

claims.claim_text: Gilead Sciences provides generic versions of long-acting medications to low- and middle-income countries for far below sticker price.
claims.subject: Gilead Sciences' provision of generics to certain countries

claims.claim_text: Gilead Sciences excludes Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and Argentina from access to affordable generics by classifying them as “upper middle-income countries.”
claims.subject: Gilead Sciences' classification of certain Latin American countries

claims.claim_text: HIV advocates dispute Gilead Sciences' justification for excluding some countries, partly because people in these countries played a key role in clinical trials to test the medications.
claims.subject: HIV advocates' dispute of Gilead's classification justification

claims.claim_text: The UNAIDS long-held goal is to eliminate AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
claims.subject: UNAIDS goal
claims.attributed_source: Beatriz Grinsztejn, president of the International Aids Society

claims.claim_text: Grinsztejn stated that it should be possible to fulfill the UNAIDS goal of eliminating AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
claims.subject: Feasibility of fulfilling the UNAIDS goal by 2030
claims.attributed_source: Beatriz Grinsztejn, president of the International Aids Society

claims.claim_text: Grinsztejn expressed doubt that the targets will be met given the current scenario.
claims.subject: Doubt about meeting AIDS elimination targets due to current scenario
claims.attributed_source: Beatriz Grinsztejn, president of the International Aids Society
